column5: Cues are not fixed in advance: the cast negotiates them in a sequence of candidate cue, confirmation, then specifying the cue. An actor who must act on a cue insists on its precise definition. Supports a rehearsal step for agreeing timing with the company.

Precise cues can lock a transition into a fixed timing. The study's best-timed transition relied on an actor's embodied action (handling a prop) to create buffer time, so timing error was absorbed. Relevant to staging transitions as well as cueing.

column4: ch-001 focus as a staging tool
column5: Director told an actor to direct the audience's focus away from a missed cue, which solved the timing. Focus is a staging tool for hiding timing variance; the article calls this an interplay of cueing and focus work.

In this production the actors, not a stage manager, were responsible for cueing; the director mostly asked questions and set the desired result. A useful example of directing as setting outcomes rather than dictating each cue. Single production, single company.
